claims.note: The non-docker production premise is this page's own ordering assumption; no file in the forqsite repository designates production as non-docker. Re-checked at forqsite commit 1fda3228 as "forqsite's production documentation still treats Postgres and MinIO as network services and compose as a development convenience". It holds: the first-run prerequisites and the runbook require Postgres and MinIO as network services reached over TCP/IP; the runbook's install and standard upgrade are pnpm build, pnpm start and a process-manager restart, not docker; architecture.md keeps single-instance installs the default and the rolling restart opt-in. The only docker production path is that opt-in rolling topology (docs/deployment/docker-compose.rolling.yml driven by scripts/rolling-restart.sh), which runs the application containers only, declares no Postgres or MinIO service, and cannot build because the repository has no Dockerfile. One discrepancy is recorded rather than hidden: the root docker-compose.yml calls itself "forqsite single-instance deployment", while no install or upgrade document routes an operator through it; "compose as a dev convenience" is the rescoping the gap list proposes, not forqsite's wording. The runbook's docker references are unchanged in count between forqsite commits 17b78645 and 1fda3228, so nothing moved toward docker and the gap ordering needs no re-sequencing.
